plaintext.source: The teleprinter copy of the same message (frame 0862, Fernschreiben of 4 June 1940, 11.45, file 249/6) is in the same file.

transcription.source: Brice Dudout's transcription of the NARA frame images by a Claude Opus agent (28 Oct 2026, before any key was known; dudout/frozen/T863-867.txt), six doubtful letters checked on the images on 12 Nov 2026; no human has checked the whole; it differs from Harumi-Matsuba's transcription in 7 of 953 letters (dudout/README.md)
transcription.notes: A hand-written radio form in five parts (179, 190, 194, 186 and 204 letters with indicator groups), one per frame; parts 1-4 in ink, part 5 in pencil in another hand. 928 letters of text without the five indicator groups, from the stated part lengths (each part checked against them).

system.summary: Double columnar transposition: plaintext written in rows in a 24-column grid, read off by the key numbers, the result written in a 28-column grid and read off the same way; the first five-letter group of each part is the indicator group and is not text; X separates words in the plaintext.

prior_solution.where: The recipient's hand-written fair copy of frame 0993 (frames 0994-0995) and the teleprinter original of frames 1025-1027 (frame 1024) are in the same file; no decipherment of the key or letter-by-letter correspondence was found.

conditions.human_role: Harumi-Matsuba set the task and the rules and directed the checks; Anthropic Claude (Claude Fable 5.1) transcribed the images, fitted the plaintext, wrote the known-plaintext tools and decrypted; OpenAI Codex read the images blind as a second reader. No human has checked the transcriptions. The project re-ran the decryption with its own code and a random-key control; it has not seen the images.

solution.what: Claude Fable 5.1 transcribed frame 0993 (read at 2,400 px and then line by line at full size) and frames 1025-1027 from the NARA images; no human has checked.
The plaintext of parts 3 and 4 of frame 0993 was fixed from the recipient's fair copy by fitting spellings (KLAMMER, STRIQ, ROEM, X as separator) to the letter counts of the parts.

Two known-plaintext searches (kpa.c, kpb.c) on part 4 gave key lengths 24 and 28 and the keys; the tools were first tested on the 1939 exercise message and key card; parts 1 and 2 of 0993 and all of frames 1025-1027 were not used and decrypt as they stand.

Contributor's controls: 1,000 random keys of the same lengths (trigram count real 66, best random 19, mean 8.7); a blind second reading by OpenAI Codex (99.2% and 93.8% to 95.4% agreement); calibration against the contemporary texts (98.8% and 91.1%).
The contributor searched this ledger, Cryptiana, Cryptoole, Schmeh's blog, GitHub and the web: nothing on the key or the messages.

Project check: an own double-transposition implementation applied to the contributor's transcriptions and keys gives the six plaintexts identical, letter for letter, to his plaintext.txt (1,023 letters); a trigram count of 66 against a mean of 8.9 and a best of 19 for 300 random key pairs (VERIFICATION.md). No image compared.
Brice Dudout: frames 0863-0867 transcribed from the NARA images by a Claude Opus agent, before any key was known (dudout/frozen/T863-867.txt).
Brice Dudout: joint annealing of both keys on quadgrams and IDP-type scores, without a crib, tried on synthetic messages of the same lengths: no key recovered, so not run on the real message.

Harumi-Matsuba: the key of 4 June 1940 for frames 0863-0867 (19 and 22 columns) from his known-plaintext tools on a candidate plaintext from frame 0862, reported on issue #364 and in his repository (commit de8efa9).
Brice Dudout: the problem sent to another model (Claude Fable 5.2, through the API) with part 4 kept back: the request was refused and nothing came back.
Brice Dudout: plaintext of parts 1 and 2 taken from frame 0862 with the 17 May conventions and fitted to the letter counts of the parts (dudout/solver/in12b.txt).

Brice Dudout, independently of Harumi-Matsuba's result: K2 by annealing on the k1-apart letter pairs (the idea of his kpb.c; own code dudout/solver/kpw.c) over k1 15-30 and k2 15-32 on parts 1-2, control on shuffled plaintext: (19, 22) alone, margin 0.174 against sd 0.019; then K1 by quadgram annealing (k1s.c) over parts 1, 2, 3 and 5. Same keys as Harumi-Matsuba's.

Brice Dudout: one pre-registered test of the frozen keys on part 4, held out (dudout/frozen/): quadgrams -4.993 per letter against -6.643 for the best of 400 controls; agreement with the plaintext predicted from frame 0862 0.989 against 0.227; pass. Declared: the raw NARA OCR of frame 0866 had been printed once before the protocol was frozen, not used.

Brice Dudout: six doubtful letters checked on the images (three n in part 1, two r and one o in part 5); the decryption reads 129 of 129 words as German sentences, 5 probable (g/q and m/n ambiguous, one letter not checked); compared letter by letter with Harumi-Matsuba's transcription: 7 differences in 953 letters.

Integration check (12 Nov 2026): an own decoder written from dudout/key_0604.txt gives the contributor's strings letter for letter on all five parts (928 letters); the frozen files' SHA-256 match; all 179 letters of frame 0863 (part 1) agree with the NARA image (parts 2-5 not compared). The read share is recounted by the README rule, which counts the 5 probable words as guessed: 124 of 129 = 0.961 (the contributor's figure, 129 of 129, is his own). The order of events (key public 11 Nov 08:28 UTC, test 23:24 CET the same day, comment found 12 Nov) rests on the contributor's record.

validation.notes: The project's n-gram test is made for substitutions; for this transposition a trigram-count control against 300 random key pairs was used (VERIFICATION.md).

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Contributor's method: the plaintext beside the ciphertext (the recipient's fair copy of frame 0993) was fitted to the letter counts and a known-plaintext search recovered the keys from part 4; the project verified that the keys decrypt all six parts with its own code, but did not repeat the search or see the images.

texts.label: Frame 0993: Luftgaukommando VII to Flugabwehrkommando Schwarzwald, 17 May 1940
texts.summary: A secret command message: Flakgruppe Friedrichshafen hands over to Flugabwehrkommando Schwarzwald the 1st and 3rd platoons of the 3rd battery of Reserve Light Flak Battalion 932 (Herbertingen), which the Flugabwehrkommando will transport and employ as arranged by telephone, and places the 3rd platoon of Anti-aircraft Machine-gun Reserve Company 304 (Sigmaringen) at the protected object Herbertingen; new positions and readiness to fire are to be reported.

reading_review.note: Read the decryption as German sentences: the six parts divide into words with the contributor's spelling conventions and match the recipient's fair copy in content; five letters are wrong as typed, and no human has checked the transcription.

texts.label: Frames 1025-1027: Flugabwehrkommando Schwarzwald Ic, 17 May 1940
texts.summary: A secret command message: on 16 May 1940 the 1st platoon of 2./932 (2 cm) of Flakgruppe Friedrichshafen was assigned to Flugabwehrkommando Schwarzwald; the platoon has been ready to fire since 22.30 hrs in position 3031 west of Tüllingen and is subordinated to Battalion 942.

reading_review.note: Read the decryption as German sentences: the two parts divide into words and match the teleprinter original in content; two hand-written letters (e or R, h or k) cannot be settled and no human has checked the transcription.

texts.label: Frames 0863-0867: Flugabwehrkommando Schwarzwald Ic, 4 June 1940
texts.summary: A secret command message: to protect army unloadings, seven Flak units of Flugabwehrkommando Schwarzwald moved into position on 3-4 June 1940 at railway stations and towns of the Black Forest (Sankt Georgen, Triberg, Peterzell, Haslach, Marbach, Hornberg, Villingen) and report the hour from which each was ready to fire; signed Flugabw.Kdo. Ic Nr. F 225/40 g.Kdos. The text is that of the teleprinter copy on frame 0862; the key of the day is the new result.

reading_review.by: Claude Opus 5.5 agent of Brice Dudout (one reader)
reading_review.note: Read the decryption as German sentences: all five parts divide into words with the 17 May conventions and agree with the teleprinter copy on frame 0862 entry by entry (places, units, hours), differing only in spelling (Sankt, zehn, ditto marks written out, a file number). 124 words certain, 5 probable on single doubtful letters (g/q, m/n, one c for e); by the README rule the probable words count as guessed, so 124 of 129 words (0.961) read. Grade A: the text builds sentences with no hole; reservation: AI transcription, no human reader, and the text was known from the teleprinter copy on frame 0862.
